newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says U.S. blocking deal to buy ambulances.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.S. blocking deal to buy ambulances.

text.p: The United States has blocked an Iraqi plan to buy 100 ambulances from France under the U.N.-approved deal to trade oil for humanitarian supplies, the Iraqi News Agency said on Tuesday.

"The American representative on the sanctions committee (on Iraq) rejected a contract with a French company to supply Iraq with 100 ambulances under the oil-for-food and humanitarian needs deal," INA said in a dispatch from New York.

The agency said Iraq wanted to import the ambulances under terms of the deal, which was intended to relieve the suffering of Iraqi civilians living under U.N. sanctions imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
"The United States has put on hold 143 medical contracts without giving any explanation for holding them," INA quoted Iraq's U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon as saying.
The Baghdad government has repeatedly blamed the United States and Britain for holding up food and medical supplies bought under the oil-for-food deal, which went into effect last December.

The agreement allowed Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion over the six months to June 8, and the Baghdad government said on Monday it would resume oil sales under the second phase of the deal within the next few days.
